title: [tenmin-redispatch] shouldDispatchHeal: characterization test for the heal-dispatch decision
body:
Target: PeaceG03/PeaceSTOCKS

add a characterization test for shouldDispatchHeal in src/tenmin-redispatch.ts: heal dispatch
- shouldDispatchHeal({ dispatch: false, nextAction: "wait", reason: "WAIT_GUARD_WINDOW", nextChain: 1 }) is true
- shouldDispatchHeal({ dispatch: false, nextAction: "wait", reason: "WAIT_NEAR_GUARD_WINDOW", nextChain: 1 }) is true
- shouldDispatchHeal({ dispatch: true, nextAction: "continue", reason: "WAIT_GUARD_WINDOW", nextChain: 1 }) is false
- shouldDispatchHeal({ dispatch: false, nextAction: "wait", reason: "OTHER", nextChain: 1 }) is false

(Builder pre-file, TEST_CASE_EXISTING, public-test-case-existing-v2): Peace's task (source: peace). The rule that only a guard-window wait triggers a heal dispatch has no direct test; this pins its current behaviour. Production safety: test-only: one new src/*.test.ts file only: no source edits, no fix commit. Job B grades it fix-free: the test passes on the current code and fails with the function body stubbed. The running scanner chain is unchanged. A box dry-run on PeaceSTOCKS 5c41528 (Workspace main efd3f76, Node 22) built exactly one candidate (public-test-case-existing-v2); a local Job B run graded it COUNTS (the new test passes on the current code and fails with shouldDispatchHeal stubbed); suite 564/564 with all eight new tests of this batch, all 4 typechecks ok. Disjoint file: each task in this batch creates its own new test file. Expected COUNTS.)
